key_insight: Source localization is reframed as a backward transport problem: detections are treated as evidence of tracer paths linking the source to the sensor locations.
engineering_relevance: This yields a single learned, Galilean-invariant propagator that can guide robust search and localization in turbulent or windy environments, relevant to robotics, sensing, and environmental monitoring.
method: Model detections with a Schrödinger bridge between emission and observation points.
Use the backward propagator of passive tracers to sample candidate source locations via Langevin dynamics.
Interpret the learned drift as a unified transport principle connecting chemotaxis and cast-and-surge behavior.
evidence_signal: In two-dimensional turbulence, the backtracking framework outperforms classical search strategies across varying wind regimes using one learned propagator.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the learned backward transport model, so mismatch between training flow statistics and the true environment could reduce localization accuracy.
paper_title: Learning Backward Transport for Source Localization
